title: The Hidden Costs of Fairness in Platform Markets: The Dynamics of Lowering Developer Royalty Rates
eligible_reason: Binary treatment (small/solo developer on a platform after that platform's royalty-cut announcement) switching on at two distinct calendar dates (iOS cohort 2020m12, Android cohort 2021m3) with a large never-treated group (incorporated/team developers); developer-platform and calendar-month FE; no covariates; clustered by unit. The reported estimator is Wooldridge's (2021) extended TWFE (jwdid, 'two-way Mundlak'), not plain TWFE: without covariates the default version equals the Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess imputation estimator and the never-treated version coincides with a Callaway-Sant'Anna/Sun-Abraham never-treated comparison, so the paper is treated as a modern-estimator report of an eligible design with a constructible TWFE counterpart. FLAG: jwdid is not on the protocol's named list; lead to confirm. Table 6 col 1 is a plain TWFE (reghdfe) on a related hunter panel and is included as borderline.
design_notes: Two platform-specific announcements of royalty cuts for small developers (Apple Nov 2020, Google Mar 2021). Developer-platform monthly panels: Product Hunt/Crunchbase (panel_id; 'treatment' = team_size==1) and AppTweak game apps (pi; small_developer). Each unit observed 12 months before, the month of, and 12 months after its platform's announcement (iOS 2019m11-2021m11; Android 2020m2-2022m2); gvar = month after announcement (2020m12 / 2021m3), 0 for never-treated. jwdid y, ivar() tvar(edate) gvar(gvar) [never] cluster(); estat simple (Tables 2-3; Panel A with never, Panel B without) and estat event + jwdid_plot (Figures 3-4). Outcomes are 0/1 launch indicators (any app; low-quality: bottom-quartile upvotes/ratings, self-hunted, zero downloads; high-quality: top-quartile upvotes/ratings/downloads, externally certified; turned into (funded) startup). Table 4: cross-section reghdfe with post x quality interactions (no unit FE). Table 5: ppmlhdfe Poisson on cumulative downloads with post x ASO-investment indicators. Tables 6-7: hunter-platform panel, reghdfe dmax_exp##post (Table 6) and triple interactions with product_hunted_dummy (Table 7), absorb(edate#ios hunter_platform).
estimators_reported: Wooldridge (2021) extended TWFE / two-way Mundlak via jwdid, static (estat simple) with never-treated controls (Panel A) and never+not-yet-treated controls (Panel B)
modern_estimators_named: Wooldridge (2021) ETWFE / two-way Mundlak (jwdid) -- equivalent to BJS imputation (default) and to CSA/Sun-Abraham never-treated (never option) without covariates; Callaway-Sant'Anna, Goodman-Bacon and de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille cited per full-text flags

data_access_note: Final de-identified analysis datasets are shipped in full; underlying raw sources (Product Hunt, AppTweak, Crunchbase) are proprietary and not shared.
data_files: Replication_Package/final_datasets_for_regressions_figures/AppTweak_developer_platform_panel.dta (496,400 unit-months; 19 vars incl. gvar; Table 3, Figures 2 and 4)
Stata log files of all regressions in Replication_Package/log_regressions_figures/*.smcl (contain the published point estimates)
software_detail: Stata 18 (jwdid, reghdfe, ftools, ppmlhdfe, estout/sutex, grc1leg)
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Only 2 adoption cohorts, each tied to a platform, so cohort = platform x small-developer status; never-treated units are large/incorporated developers on the same platforms. Calendar windows differ by platform (iOS Nov 2019-Nov 2021; Android Feb 2020-Feb 2022) but overlap, so edate FE are identified across platforms. Published coefficients can be recovered from the shipped .smcl logs (Log_Fig1_Fig3_Tab1PanelA_Tab2.smcl, Log_Fig2_Fig4_Tab1PanelB_Tab3.smcl, Log_Table6_Table7.smcl) pending the article PDF. Inclusion hinges on accepting jwdid/ETWFE as a modern-estimator report; if rejected, the only plain-TWFE candidate is the borderline Table 6 col 1.
lead_ruling: 2026-11-01 (team lead): Tables 2-3 and Figures 3-4 report only Wooldridge's extended TWFE (Stata jwdid), which is not on the protocol's admitted list (TWFE, Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham when coinciding with CSA, Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess, did2s). Table 6 column 1 is a plain reghdfe regression (product_hunted_dummy on c.dmax_exp##c.post with hunter-platform FE and year-month x platform FE, no controls) but its regressor of interest is the interaction of a time-invariant hunter attribute (experienced hunter) with the platform-wide post-announcement indicator, i.e. a subgroup-by-post heterogeneity term ('by hunter experience' in the table title) rather than a unit-level adoption of the royalty-cut treatment; excluded under the subgroup-by-treatment-interaction rule. No spec JSONs kept; the 25 candidate specs were replicated exactly and archived in ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2024.05861/archived_specs/ and archived_output/ (see data/replication_logs/mnsc.2024.05861.md).
